key_insight: Sparse neural networks identify compact hyperelastic strain-energy models while exposing individual invariant contributions and their interactions.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports interpretable constitutive model identification for describing nonlinear elastic material behavior.
method: Represent strain-energy density as a sum of products of univariate invariant functions.
Apply sparsity-promoting constraints and regularization to retain few active modes.
Identify models in supervised and unsupervised learning settings.
evidence_signal: Synthetic-data demonstrations in both learning settings show accurate, interpretable model identification with few active modes.
watch_item: The abstract reports only synthetic-data validation, so robustness to experimental noise and real-material complexity remains unestablished.
paper_title: Sparse Constitutive Neural Networks for Hyperelasticity
